messages.author: ba017c04198b2fc9
messages.subject: Invalid period with Actiwatch .csv
parts:
Hello everyone and thank you to anyone kind enough to answer my question.
I was given a set of recordings made a few years ago with Philips Actiwatch actigraphs. Unfortunately, I don't have the sleep diaries. I did a test with one of the recordings, the file is read correctly but there is an error I cannot correct in the way GGIR reads the periods of nonwear immediately before bedtime. In fact, the time in bed is over-estimated and this affects both the SPT value (which also includes the aforementioned nonwear periods) and the WASO.
I have tried different ways of handling the missing values (which on my csv are indicated as ‘NaN’) and also manually setting the guider but nothing changes.
Alternatively, I could also calculate sleep measures with the philips software and use GGIR only for circadian parameters but I am afraid that even those would be distorted.

I attach one of the different parameter combinations I used and the test file I am working on, thank you very much for your help.

Marco

GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4),
     do.report=c(2,4),
     datadir = "C:\\Users\\marcv\\Desktop\\prova\\input",
     outputdir = "C:\\Users\\marcv\\Desktop\\prova\\output",
     dataFormat = "actiwatch_csv",
     extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",
     windowsizes = c(30, 900, 3600),
     HASIB.algo = "Sadeh1994",
     HASPT.ignore.invalid=TRUE,
     ignorenonwear=TRUE,
     def.noc.sleep = c(22,8),
     do.imp=FALSE,
     overwrite=TRUE)

messages.author: ba017c04198b2fc9
messages.subject: Re: Invalid period with Actiwatch .csv
parts:
I also tried to modify the parameter windowsize to (30,900,1800) but in only led to wrong nonwear period during the night.
I saw from the test files that there are "excluded" period, so I think that exporting the csv after a first manual scoring on Philips software is correct.
maybe I could manually preprocess the csv to change "NaN" period in some label that the imputation function of GGIR recognize as invalid epoch, but I wasn't able to understand from the code which is the correct label to set.

Thank you so much

Marco

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Invalid period with Actiwatch .csv
parts:
Hi Marco,

If I understand correctly your concern is about the nonwear detection. I agree that shortening the windowsizes was worth trying.

If you manually set the guider via a sleeplog  then consider also setting parameter relyonguider = TRUE, which forces GGIR to use the guider for defining onset and wakeup time.

I am not sure what 'excluded' periods means in the context of Actiwatch data. If the test file gives the impression that GGIR facilitates handling them then probably this a misunderstanding as I was not aware that Actiwatch files can come with 'excluded' periods. I would be happy to discuss opportunities for enhancing GGIR to better handle those excluded periods as part of a paid consultancy, but that will have to wait until after I am back from travelling (17th of February).

Thanks,

Vincent

parts:
Hi Vincent, thank you so much for your answer.
Yes, with actiwatch, and usually with other activity counts devices, you can select intervals to exclude from the actogram and when you export the csv with epoch by epoch data in the column "activity" you'll find "NaN" or "na" ecc..
I saw that GGIR translate those epochs in 0 activity count, and then in sleep epochs. I would be happy to discuss with you about this issue. Please feel free to write me for a quote and if it's affordable for me we can arrange to meet after Feb. 17

Thank you 

Marco
